rounds.question: Name a cause of rapid industrialization after the Civil War

answers.explanation: This is a cause of industrialization — the US had vast iron, coal, and timber needed for factories and railroads.
This is a cause of industrialization — railroads created a national market, moving raw materials and finished goods efficiently.
This is a cause of industrialization — millions of immigrants provided cheap labor for factories, mines, and construction.
This is a cause of industrialization — innovations like the Bessemer process, telephone, and electric light powered economic growth.
This is a cause of industrialization — high tariffs, land grants, and laissez-faire policies gave corporations enormous advantages.

rounds.question: Name a problem caused by the rise of big business and trusts

answers.explanation: This is a problem of big business — trusts and monopolies drove out competitors, leaving consumers and workers with no alternatives.

answers.text: Low wages and poor conditions for workers
answers.explanation: This is a problem of big business — corporations maximized profits by minimizing labor costs, ignoring worker safety.
This is a problem of big business — robber barons bribed legislators and controlled political machines at every level.
This is a problem of big business — without competition, monopolies could charge whatever they wanted for essential goods.
This is a problem of big business — Standard Oil and similar trusts used predatory pricing to eliminate smaller rivals.

rounds.question: Name a reason immigrants came to the United States in the late 1800s

answers.explanation: This is a reason immigrants came to the US — the 'pull' of factory jobs and land was powerful compared to conditions in Europe.
This is a reason immigrants came to the US — famine in Ireland, poverty in Southern Italy, and persecution in Eastern Europe pushed millions out.
This is a reason immigrants came to the US — Jews fleeing pogroms, political dissidents, and religious minorities all sought refuge.
This is a reason immigrants came to the US — the promise of the American Dream, however imperfect, drew people across the Atlantic.
This is a reason immigrants came to the US — chain migration meant earlier arrivals sent letters home encouraging others to follow.

rounds.question: Name a response to the problems of industrialization

answers.explanation: This is a response to industrialization — the 1890 law gave the federal government power to break up monopolistic trusts.
This is a response to industrialization — workers organized the Knights of Labor, AFL, and others to demand better conditions.
This is a response to industrialization — it created the first federal regulatory agency, aimed at controlling railroad rates.
This is a response to industrialization — major strikes like Homestead and Pullman brought national attention to labor conditions.
This is a response to industrialization — journalists like Upton Sinclair and Ida Tarbell turned public opinion against big business.

rounds.question: Name a hardship faced by immigrants arriving in the late 1800s

answers.explanation: This is a hardship immigrants faced — factories had no safety regulations; injuries and deaths were common and uncompensated.
This is a hardship immigrants faced — 'old stock' Americans opposed new immigrants from Southern and Eastern Europe.
This is a hardship immigrants faced — urban slums were dangerously overcrowded, with poor sanitation and disease.
This is a hardship immigrants faced — non-English speakers were exploited by employers and struggled to navigate daily life.
This is a hardship immigrants faced — 12-hour days, six days a week, for poverty wages was the norm in Gilded Age factories.

rounds.question: Name a tactic used by workers to improve conditions

answers.explanation: This is a worker tactic — refusing to work was the labor movement's most powerful tool to force employer concessions.
This is a worker tactic — collective organization gave workers bargaining power they could never have had individually.
This is a worker tactic — unions negotiated wages, hours, and conditions on behalf of all workers, not just individuals.
This is a worker tactic — consumer pressure through boycotts was used alongside strikes to hurt company profits.
This is a worker tactic — unions pushed for legislation like the eight-hour workday and child labor bans.
